## science_fiction_concept_keyframe

> Cinematic sci-fi keyframe matte painting — alien landscape or far-future urban scene with painterly atmosphere.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1920x1088`, aspect `16:9`
**Demo vars:** `templates/science_fiction_concept/_vars_examples/science_fiction_concept_keyframe.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A cinematic science-fiction keyframe matte painting depicting a abandoned tidal megacity dominated by a kilometer-tall ringed orbital lift. The frame is a single composed concept-art plate, not a 3D-CG render and not a photograph. The scale of the focal object against the surrounding environment establishes the world's tone in one read. No real-world locations, no recognizable IP, no on-screen UI elements.
[2. Action] The viewer's eye enters along the strongest atmospheric gradient, rides into the deep middle ground, then settles on the focal object silhouette. A small footer label later anchors the location for the art department. The frame should feel like a still pulled from a longer film, not a hero poster.
[3. Scene] abandoned tidal megacity, charged by an atmosphere of monsoon dust haze and rust-orange dawn. Aerial perspective is doing real work — clear foreground, hazed mid-ground, dissolved background. Optional aerial particulates (dust, ash, ion spray) sell the scale. Single dominant key light source; ambient fill is muted and color-coherent.
[4. Composition] Wide 16:9 plate, 4% safe margins. The horizon sits on a deliberate third — low for grandeur, high for claustrophobia. The focal object is offset from center along the rule-of-thirds; negative atmospheric space takes the rest. A small footer slug occupies the bottom 4% holding the scene label. Aerial perspective and silhouette discipline do the depth work, not lens-flare gimmicks.
[5. Style] Painterly concept-art register in the lineage of Syd Mead, Ralph McQuarrie, Sparth and Maciej Kuciara — visible brushwork in the midtones, restrained palette anchored on rust orange, ash grey, distant cyan, cinematic but never glossy CG-plastic. Edges suggest geometry rather than render every rivet. No real-IP ships, no real-place skylines, no photoreal HDR gloss.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- scene_label: "abandoned tidal megacity - kilometer-tall ringed orbital lift"

NO: 3D-CG plastic gloss, photoreal HDR finish, real-IP spaceships, real public figures, real city skylines, on-screen HUD overlays, lens flare, rainbow gradients, watermarks, stock-photo cutouts
```

## science_fiction_concept_vehicle_hero

> Hero side-view concept-art plate of a fictional sci-fi vehicle, mech, or spacecraft on a clean studio plate.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1920x1088`, aspect `16:9`
**Demo vars:** `templates/science_fiction_concept/_vars_examples/science_fiction_concept_vehicle_hero.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A hero side-view concept rendering of a fictional long-haul cargo lifter bearing the designation HELIOS-VII / CL-44 MULE from the post-corporate frontier-utility era era. The vehicle is the only subject — no pilots, no scenery, no competing props — composed as a single readable silhouette so the art department can lock the form before color and detail passes. No real-IP designs, no licensed franchise marks.
[2. Action] The viewer reads the silhouette first, then the proportional relationships of cockpit-to-engine-to-armament, then the surface detail. The designation slug sits unobtrusively below the hull like a hangar plate. The frame must survive being printed in a callsheet at A4.
[3. Scene] Clean studio concept-art plate. The vehicle floats above a soft ground-shadow on a flat color field appropriate to the post-corporate frontier-utility era — neutral mid-grey for utility eras, off-white for clean-room eras, charcoal for grimdark eras. No environment, no parallax, no diorama dressing.
[4. Composition] Wide 16:9 plate, 5% safe margins. The vehicle is rendered in strict orthographic side view, occupying the central ~70% of the frame, baseline aligned to a notional hangar floor at ~60% height. A thin technical-callout rule may run beneath the hull; the designation label sits in the lower-right corner like a spec-sheet stamp. No three-quarter glamour angle, no in-flight drama.
[5. Style] Industrial concept-art register tuned to post-corporate frontier-utility era — silhouette- first design discipline of Ryan Church, Doug Chiang, John Park and Ash Thorp. Restrained palette anchored on warm sand, oxide red, gunmetal grey, matte material reads, painterly brushwork in panel transitions. Not 3D-CG plastic, not photoreal, not chromed showroom render.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- vehicle_designation: "HELIOS-VII / CL-44 MULE"

NO: 3D-CG plastic gloss, photoreal showroom chrome, real-IP spaceships, real military insignia, in-cockpit pilots, background environments, lens flare, rainbow gradients, watermarks, HUD overlays
```
